title: Breguet and the invention of the tourbillon

slides.title: Built for a problem your watch *barely has.*
slides.body: Abraham-Louis Breguet's most famous invention, and the debate it still sparks 225 years later.

image.credit: Abraham-Louis Breguet, c. 1810 · Unknown painter · Public domain

slides.title: Gravity in your *pocket*
slides.body: Pocket watches spent hours upright in a waistcoat. Gravity pulled on the balance in the same direction all day, **and the watch drifted.**

slides.title: A cage that *rotates*
slides.body: On 26 June 1801, “7 Messidor, Year IX” in France's revolutionary calendar, Breguet patents the **tourbillon**: the escapement spins in a cage, averaging out gravity's errors.

image.credit: Breguet's original drawing for the 1801 patent · Public domain

slides.title: Only *35* sold
slides.body: Breguet sold just 35 tourbillons in his lifetime. And most didn't turn once a minute, as the patent describes, **but every 4 or 6 minutes.**

slides.title: A tribute to a *friend*
slides.body: Breguet gives Arnold's son a chronometer by his late friend John Arnold, fitted with what its plaque calls *“the first tourbillon regulator by Breguet.”* **It's now in the British Museum.**

slides.title: Does it work on the *wrist?*
slides.body: A wristwatch already moves through countless positions, so many experts say a tourbillon adds little accuracy. **Today it's mostly a showcase of skill.**

image.credit: A modern tourbillon cage · Photo: Guy Sie · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: The queen's *impossible watch*
slides.body: It has no tourbillon, but everything else: an officer orders it for Marie Antoinette with **no limit on time or cost.** Guillotined in 1793, she never saw it finished.

image.credit: Breguet No. 160 “Marie-Antoinette”, Jerusalem · Photo: Atzatz · CC BY-SA 4.0

slides.title: Stolen, then *returned*
slides.body: The watch is stolen from a museum in Jerusalem. **More than twenty years later**, it comes back through a lawyer acting for the thief's widow.

slides.title: Invented for pockets. *Admired on wrists.*
slides.next: Paul Newman's Daytona and the auction record

caption:
In 1801, Breguet invented a spinning cage to fight gravity. 225 years later, it's still watchmaking's ultimate flex. 🌀

The tourbillon was designed for pocket watches stuck upright in a waistcoat. Breguet sold only 35 in his lifetime, and experts still debate whether it helps a wristwatch at all.

Would you buy a tourbillon? 👇

Sources: Breguet archive; Swatch Group archive; Revolution; British Museum; Quill & Pad; Wikipedia.
